 ORDER

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.22 of 2024 registered at Police Station Bhitarwar, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376 and 450 of IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 16.01.2024.

A s per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix aged around 35 years submitted a written complaint to SHO, PS- Bhitarwar on 14.01.2024 that previous day i.e. 13.01.2024, her husband and son had gone out for some work.
Her mother-in-law had gone to local market and her daughters were working in the agricultural field.
She was alone sitting in front of her house.
An unknown person came and asked about her husband.
When she went inside the house, that unknown person entered her house and committed rape on her.
Thereafter, the person fled away.
Hearing her shout, her neighbour came to her house.
She narrated the incident.

Some unknown person was calling from mobile Ramniwas @ Bhonda vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101172668/

sentences.text: She called her husband and informed about the incident.

On such allegation, PS- Bhitarwar registered FIR at Crime No.
22/2024 for offence punishable under Sections 376 and 450 of IPC.
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico legal examination.
No external or internal injury was found.
No definite opinion was given by the medical expert with regard to forceful sexual assault.
Statement of prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 of CrPC.
Applicant was arrested on 16.01.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
In Test Identification Parade, prosecutrix identified the applicant as assailant.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 14.02.2024.
FSL and DNA Report are still awaited.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter due to pressure of family members of the complainant.
Applicant and prosecutrix had been communicating on mobile phone regularly.
Learned counsel referring to call detail reports submitted with charge-sheet contends that even on the date of alleged incident, applicant and the prosecutrix were communicating on mobile phone.
This fact along with delayed FIR substantiate false implication after pre-meditation.
Learned counsel submits that applicant is aged 41 years.
He is agriculturist and has a family to look after.
He is sole bread earner of the family.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with evidence as both the parties relate to same socio- economic status.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel further submits that FSL and DNA Report are still awaited which will clear the air.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
